findings.forcedInvention: Who owns paid/promoted discovery, user onboarding and activation, and the referral/affiliate system — and whether 'follow / save / watchlist' is one shared primitive or a per-domain feature. Nothing in the root unit answers any of these, so an implementer must invent the owner, the shape, and whether the capability exists at all.
findings.claim: The 32 cross-cutting systems ratified in domain-map-proposal.md (D-16) were consolidated to the 25-mechanism registry in ideation-cx.md, and at least three of them vanished entirely: they appear in no registry row, in no §1b unratified-candidate row, and in no row of the not-product downstream-routing table. 'Promoted Placement & Advertising' has zero trace anywhere in the root unit or in any of the 734 ledger feature titles. 'Onboarding & Role-Aware Activation' survives only as the unrelated string 'KYC/KYB onboarding' inside the Payments row. 'Referrals, Invites & Affiliates' survives only as unrelated per-domain prose. 'Follow, Save & Watchlist' has zero occurrences in ideation-cx.md or ideation-index.md, yet the ledger already carries at least three independent per-domain implementations (03.01.01 'Follows (Asymmetric)', 20.06.01 'Artist Tracking & Follow', 22.07.01 'Artist Watchlists') — which is precisely the outcome §1b says the registry exists to prevent. Both structures that assert completeness are therefore incomplete: the registry claims to be the consolidated set, and §1b claims to hold everything not promoted into it.

findings.failure_scenario: An implementer builds domain 13 (Gear Marketplace, a v1.5 domain). The ratified cross-cut table says 'Follow, Save & Watchlist' is a shared primitive serving 13 alongside 03/04/11/14/16/20, and that 'Promoted Placement & Advertising' governs paid discovery for 13. The consolidated 25-mechanism registry contains neither, and the not-product table routes neither to /create-prd. Implementer A follows the registry, builds a domain-local 'watch this listing' table, and ships no promoted listings — so gear watchlists cannot be surfaced beside the 20.06.01 artist-follow feed and the marketplace has no monetization surface. Implementer B follows the ratified proposal, builds a shared interest primitive and a promoted-placement auction with disclosure rules. Both are defensible from the root unit and the two systems are schema-incompatible. For 'Promoted Placement & Advertising' specifically there is no source anywhere — no mechanism row, no candidate row, no routing row, and no feature among all 734 — so its disclosure obligations (a legal requirement for paid discovery) are invented from nothing or silently dropped.

findings.claim: domain-map-proposal.md asserts a `**Personas.**` field on all 24 domain sections, using 99 distinct persona tokens, with no qualifier anywhere in the file and no reconciliation note in any root file. This directly collides with the locked persona model: D-19 fixes exactly 4 primary personas, the Progress Summary asserts '0 invented personas', and D-71 spends an entire decision establishing that non-persona commercial actors must NOT be called personas — creating meta/counterparties.md specifically so they are not. Several actors D-71 names as explicitly still-open non-personas are listed here as personas without qualification: 'dealer/shop' (:60, :204 — D-71's personas.md Q-01), 'moderator' (:336 — D-71's personas.md Q-02), 'insurer' (:228), 'accountant'/'financial advisor' (:324), 'parent/guardian' (:120). D-35 subordinates this file's *structure* to the folder tree but says nothing about its persona assertions, and the file's own scope disclaimer at :7 covers folders and scope only.

findings.failure_scenario: An implementer building the Role Matrix for domain 24 (Trust, Safety & Disputes) reads domain-map-proposal.md:336 and provisions 8 persona columns including 'moderator' and 'reported user'. D-71 states that Admin/Moderator is an explicitly OPEN question (personas.md Q-02, vision.md Q-00) with no persona and no Role Matrix column, and D-19 permits only 4. The implementer either ships a 4-column matrix that silently drops the moderator the domain is built around, or ships an 8-column matrix that invents a persona the owner has twice declined to ratify — and the same fork repeats across all 24 domains, since every section carries this field.

findings.claim: moscow-ledger.md's header states the release-sequencing position that ideation-index.md explicitly records as superseded, and carries no amendment marker or pointer to the superseding decision. The index strikes through exactly this clause inside D-20 and states in terms that /plan-phase 'no longer needs to pick a beachhead'. The ledger states the opposite as live fact.

The beachhead is chosen (v1 = the spine); `/plan-phase` sequences the ~45 v1 Musts, then the ~26 v1.5 Musts. It no longer needs to pick a beachhead — D-31 did.'
findings.failure_scenario: A /plan-phase run opens moscow-ledger.md — the file that actually enumerates all 195 Musts and is therefore the natural starting point for sequencing — reads line 4, and treats beachhead selection as its own open decision. It sequences all 195 Musts by global dependency order rather than ordering within the D-31 releases, producing a phase plan that ignores the v1 = 45-Must session spine and the v1.5 = 26-Must marketplace split, and thereby reintroduces the exact solo/3-6-month over-scope risk D-29 was superseded to fix.

findings.claim: The consolidated mechanism registry's `Serves` list for Realtime Rooms, Presence & Audio Transport omits domain 05 Services Marketplace, while the ratified decision that created this mechanism names Services as one of the four domains it was extracted to serve. Neither statement carries a marker, and no root file reconciles them. This matters for scope rather than presentation: 05 Services is a v1 domain under D-31 while 08 Real-Time Jamming is phase-2, so whether a paid Services engagement can host a realtime room is a v1 build question.
findings.evidence: ideation-cx.md:31 — '| **Realtime Rooms, Presence & Audio Transport** | 08 | 03,06,07,08,17,18 | Low-latency realtime rooms with presence, collaborative-editing state, and synchronized audio/media transport for jamming and remote sessions. |' (Serves = 03,06,07,08,17,18 — no 05)  ||  ideation-index.md:201 (D-15) — 'Audio transport extracted into the `Real-Time Rooms, Presence & Audio Transport` cross-cut (**serves Education, Services, Projects, Community**) — this concedes the strongest adversarial objection.' (Education=06, Services=05, Projects=07, Community=03)  ||  ideation-index.md:74 establishes the registry as authoritative — '| Cross-cut mechanisms (consolidated registry) | **25** — in `ideation-cx.md` |'
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer specifying domain 05 (Services Marketplace, v1) must decide whether a booked remote mixing or session-player engagement can open a realtime monitored room. Reading D-15 — a ratified owner decision whose stated justification for extracting the mechanism at all is that it serves Services — they wire 05 to the realtime cross-cut and pull a phase-2 capability into v1. Reading the consolidated registry's Serves column they do not, and 05 engagements are file-exchange only. The two v1 products differ in whether the marketplace supports live remote sessions, and neither reading is marked as superseded.

findings.claim: D-75's tracked open question carries an owner marker but no deferral target, which is malformed against the convention the same Decision Log uses everywhere else (D-72 defers to `/create-prd-security`, D-38/D-47 defer to a named validation packet, ideation-cx.md §1b gives every candidate a 'Target stage' column). The question asks whether the newly-created five-value `domains` axis is the same vocabulary as domain 17's ratified work-type enum or a fourth vocabulary, and flags a live conflict between two sources over whether `sync` sits inside publishing or beside it — but names no stage that must rule, so no downstream workflow is obligated to pick it up.
findings.evidence: ideation-index.md:260 (D-75) — 'Tracked, unresolved — **[OWNER]**: are the five domains identical to domain 17\'s ratified work-type enum, or a fourth vocabulary? `01.03.02`:25 lists **sync** as publishing\'s *sibling* while `09.01.04`:102 carves sync *inside* publishing as a right type (performance, mechanical, sync, print); this needs a taxonomy ruling and is not answered here.'  ||  Contrast the well-formed pattern in the same table, ideation-index.md:257 (D-72) — 'the **US instrument names are deferred to `/create-prd-security`** because no ideation source contains them, keeping a LIVE `[PENDING]` in 16.01.06.'  ||  Contrast ideation-cx.md:47 (§1b column header) — '| Candidate | Provisional owner | Serves | Deciding question | **Target stage** |'  ||  ideation-index.md:158 asserts this never happens — '| 7 | Open Question Resolution | ✅ | Every open question has owner + target stage (pipeline-stage = deadline).'
findings.failure_scenario: /create-prd and /decompose-architecture both run without a named owner-stage for the taxonomy ruling, so neither treats it as theirs. Domain 01 ships a `domains` enum of five values with `sync` beside `publishing`, domain 09 ships a right-type enum with `sync` inside `publishing`, and domain 17 ships its work-type enum as a third list. A representation edge granted `publishing` then resolves differently at a 09 call site than at an 01 call site — the AND-at-the-call-site rule D-75 locks becomes non-deterministic for exactly the right type (sync) the conflict names.
